Subject: Vector store interoperability consortium — technical kickoff & compliance plan

Hi everyone,

Thanks for the quick alignment on the commercial side last week. I wanted to put a short technical & compliance kickoff on the table to make sure the pilot we proposed for BigRetail is practical across vendor stacks (Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector on S3).

High-level ask: can each vendor confirm the minimum integration surface we'll need for a multi-store fallthrough architecture and provide the following by EOD Monday:
- a short note on prefix KV/cache semantics for streamed generation workloads
- max recommended vector dimension and payload size limits for production workloads
- any network/topology constraints (VPC peering, outbound TLS policies, port requirements)
- SOC2 / contractual evidence we need to collect for the pilot

Attached is a draft SOW and an initial test matrix (interop-test-matrix.csv). The SOW is intentionally light on commercial terms — Marissa, Olga and Priyom are looped for scope & redlines.

Proposed next steps:
1) vendors share the items above by Mon 2027-06-14
2) 30m cross-vendor technical sync (week of 2027-06-21)
3) 2-week sandbox pilot with common dataset + pass/fail criteria defined in test matrix

Amit — as BigRetail's engineering lead, please confirm available windows for the sync and any compliance contacts we should include.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-interop-sow-v1.2.pdf, interop-test-matrix.csv
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@pinecone.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sara Müller <sara.mueller@weaviate.com>, Amit Jain <amit.jain@bigretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vector store interoperability consortium — technical kickoff & compliance plan

Karthik,

Appreciate the outline — Pinecone is in and we can provide the items requested. Quick notes from our side:
- Prefix/KV: we treat metadata payloads as opaque and support per-vector metadata (JSON) with indexed fields. For streaming generation, our prefix caching is best-effort; we recommend keeping large prefix material in a separate blob store (S3) and storing vector references.
- Dimensions & payload: up to 2048 dims recommended; payload per vector should be < 64KB to avoid IO amplification during upserts.
- Network: standard TLS 1.2+ outbound; we can support IP allowlisting or VPC peering for Dedicated accounts (requires an infra ticket).
- Compliance: we'll provide a SOC2 attestation PDF; for the pilot that should be sufficient. For production contracts we can share our security questionnaire answers.

I'll attach our short tech note as a follow-up. Also — we have a published interoperability note that maps S3-backed pgvector fallthrough patterns to Pinecone indexing: https://pinecone.io/docs/interop-fallthrough (this is a concise guide, not exhaustive).

Liam
Senior Solutions Engineer
Pinecone

Karthik — quick commercial/ops notes from my side after reading the draft SOW:
- Timeline: remove hard production dates; mark pilot as 'technical validation' and allow 3 business days for vendor onboarding.
- Liability: tighten the data residency clause for EU data; add a clause that prohibits vendors from using payloads for model training (customer-provided data).
- Acceptance criteria: add an explicit perf bucket for tail-latency during mixed read/write workloads (see section 3.2).

I've attached a redline (redwood-interop-sow-v1.2-redlines.docx). Also — to satisfy BigRetail's security team we will need either the vendor SOC2 PDFs or completed security questionnaires. Olga — can you follow up to request Pinecone's and Weaviate's questionnaire exports and push for answers to the key network questions? Priyom — can you own the test harness integration and confirm we can run the matrix against a single combined dataset?

Marissa
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
